heading: Sun Prairie Approves 2027 Budget on 5-3 Vote
summary: The Sun Prairie Common Council approved the city's amended 2027 budget on a 5-3 vote. One amendment added $50,000 from expenditure restraint funds to the nonprofit funding pool, passing 5-3. Staff said that additional nonprofit funding is for 2027, with support for 2028 to be considered in the next budget cycle.

heading: Council Approves Wastewater and Stormwater Fee Increases
summary: The Sun Prairie Common Council approved a 9.9% increase in wastewater fees and a 3.5% increase in stormwater fees. Staff clarified that the stormwater increase amounts to 57 cents per month, correcting an amount in the initial resolution. The council approved both measures, with the stormwater increase passing 8-0.

heading: Colonial Club Wins $130,000 in Emergency Funding
summary: The Sun Prairie Common Council voted 6-2 to award the Colonial Club $130,000 in emergency support from the 2027 nonprofit funding pool. Club representatives said the money would support staff and services for older adults during the first half of 2027. Opponents questioned whether the club should draw on its reserves, while supporters cited the effect of the city's changed nonprofit funding process. A club representative said it would seek another $130,000 for the rest of 2027 through the regular application process.

heading: Council Reserves $30,000 for Possible Polling Place Changes
summary: The Sun Prairie Common Council approved setting aside $30,000 in the 2027 budget for a possible increase in polling locations. The amendment protects funding while the city considers expanding from four locations to eight. Council members discussed long election lines and the need for a recommendation from the city clerk. Changing the number or location of polling places would require a later council decision through an ordinance.

heading: Sun Prairie Adopts State Legislative Priorities
summary: The Sun Prairie Common Council adopted a resolution establishing the city's priorities for the next Wisconsin legislative session. The priorities seek relief from municipal levy limits, more options for local revenue, increased shared revenue and transportation aid, and authority to create a regional transit authority. The council approved the version amended earlier that evening by the Committee of the Whole to include local control over data center development and repeal of the state constitution's same-sex marriage ban.

heading: Mural Fest Organizers Report 18 New Murals in Two Years
summary: Mural Fest organizers told Sun Prairie's Committee of the Whole that the festival brought 18 new murals to the city in its first two years. Nine murals went on a Washington Mills factory wall in 2025, followed by nine more at locations around downtown in the second year. Organizers said the project brought residents, businesses and artists together through public painting activities and daily visits to watch artists work. They also described tourism benefits and said they were looking ahead to a third year in 2027.

heading: Sun Prairie Utilities Says Billing Review Will Take Years
summary: Sun Prairie Utilities staff told the Utilities Commission that they had completed billing reviews for 17 accounts and expected the broader review to take years. The work checks current charges and past bills, with corrections requiring additional time after errors are identified. Staff cited cases in which flat water charges continued after meters were installed. They said they are correcting problems as they go and working to improve communication between field crews and billing staff.

heading: Utilities Commission Backs Continued Participation in PFAS Settlements
summary: The Sun Prairie Utilities Commission recommended that the Common Council keep the utility in another group of PFAS class action settlements. Staff said participation follows the utility's earlier decision to join related litigation in 2023. The newer settlements could reimburse some costs of testing water for PFAS, with smaller payments expected than from the original settlements. Staff said updated pumping and testing information would be needed and that the recommendation would go to the council for a decision.

heading: Wisconsin DOJ Highlights Scam Warning Signs
summary: Wisconsin Attorney General Josh Kaul and Wausau law enforcement highlighted financial scams during International Fraud Awareness Week. The Wisconsin Department of Justice said scammers often impersonate government agencies, banks, tech support or loved ones and pressure people to act quickly or keep a transaction secret. Kaul urged people facing those demands to pause and independently check the story before handing over money. The department pointed residents to its Stop Financial Scams flyer and said suspected scams can be reported to local law enforcement or state consumer protection agencies.

heading: Wisconsin Promotes Free Quit Support Ahead of Great American Smokeout
summary: The Wisconsin Department of Health Services is highlighting free tobacco and nicotine quit support ahead of the Nov 19 Great American Smokeout. The agency said residents ages 13 and older can contact the Wisconsin Tobacco Quit Line for personalized coaching, online support and live chat. It also highlighted programs for young people who vape, Indigenous residents, pregnant residents and Medicaid members. The department encouraged people to use the annual event to take a first step, including making a quit plan.
